headline: South Korea will keep its national AI model contest going while adding a separate 4.7 trillion won frontier AI program, and experts question how the two will fit together.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a new national funding plan and a strategy debate with named experts, but the programs' details are still open.
importance_line: South Korean AI developers in the contest and the public bodies that would use national models are affected first, then taxpayers funding both tracks, but this is an announced plan, the government has not said how the two programs will divide their work, and support for finalists may change in size and form.
summary: The Korea Times reports that the Science Ministry confirmed the national AI foundation model project, a contest to build the country's own large AI models, will go on to a third evaluation with two finalists due in February, while the government plans a separate frontier AI program worth 4.7 trillion won (about $3.5 billion) from March 2027. A professor quoted says organisations are likely to prefer a frontier model once one exists and questions whether the older project is still needed, and an industry official says the two tracks could create synergies but could also confuse the three teams still competing: LG AI Research, SK Telecom and Upstage.
notes: Link is the Korea Times AMP page, as in the chunk. Minister Bae Kyung-hoon spoke at the National Assembly audit on Tuesday (6 Oct 2026); the cover story is dated 11 Oct 2026. The article names Anthropic's Claude Mythos as one reason the government says the AI landscape changed; not repeated in the summary.
